REQUIREMENT: Real-time Notification System

The system shall deliver notifications to users in a timely manner.

Notifications must be sent through appropriate channels based on user preferences.

The system should handle high volumes of notifications efficiently.

Users must be able to customize their notification settings easily.

Critical notifications require immediate delivery.

The system shall track notification delivery status reliably.

# Requirements Analysis

## Confirmed Facts
- The requirement document is titled "Real-time Notification System".
- The system shall deliver notifications to users in a timely manner.
- Notifications must be sent through appropriate channels based on user preferences.
- The system should handle high volumes of notifications efficiently.
- Users must be able to customize their notification settings easily.
- Critical notifications require immediate delivery.
- The system shall track notification delivery status reliably.

## Ambiguities
- **"in a timely manner"**
  Reason: no measurable delivery latency or SLA is defined.
- **"appropriate channels"**
  Reason: the allowed channels and selection rules are not specified.
- **"based on user preferences"**
  Reason: it is unclear how preferences are stored, prioritized, or resolved when multiple preferences conflict.
- **"handle high volumes of notifications efficiently"**
  Reason: no throughput, scaling, or performance targets are given.
- **"easily"**
  Reason: usability expectations are subjective and not testable as written.
- **"Critical notifications"**
  Reason: the criteria for classifying a notification as critical are not defined.
- **"immediate delivery"**
  Reason: no exact delivery window or fallback behavior is stated.
- **"track notification delivery status reliably"**
  Reason: the required status states, update timing, and reliability guarantees are unspecified.

## Clarification Questions
- What delivery latency or SLA defines "timely manner"?
- Which notification channels are supported, and how should the system choose among them?
- How should user preferences be stored and resolved when multiple channels are enabled?
- What volume, throughput, or concurrency targets must the system meet?
- What does "easily" mean for customizing notification settings, and are there UX or accessibility requirements?
- What makes a notification "critical"?
- What is the required delivery window for "immediate delivery"?
- Which delivery status values must be tracked, and what reliability expectations apply?

## Assumptions
- If nobody answers, developers will assume "timely" means best-effort near-real-time delivery without a formal SLA.
- If nobody answers, developers will assume the system supports only the channels already implemented or most commonly used in the product.
- If nobody answers, developers will assume user preferences are a simple per-user configuration with straightforward precedence rules.
- If nobody answers, developers will assume performance should be good enough for expected production traffic but without a published benchmark.
- If nobody answers, developers will assume "easily" means a standard settings UI with no special usability acceptance criteria.
- If nobody answers, developers will assume "critical" notifications are those flagged by the sender or originating service.
- If nobody answers, developers will assume "immediate delivery" means highest-priority dispatch with no intentional delay.
- If nobody answers, developers will assume delivery status tracking includes basic states such as queued, sent, delivered, and failed.

## Summary
The requirement describes a real-time notification system with preference-based channel selection, support for high notification volumes, user-configurable settings, immediate handling for critical notifications, and delivery status tracking. However, the document does not define measurable performance, channel, classification, or reliability criteria, so several implementation details still need clarification before work can start.

# Requirements Analysis

## Confirmed Facts
- The requirement document is titled "Real-time Notification System".
- The system shall deliver notifications to users in a timely manner.
- Notifications must be sent through appropriate channels based on user preferences.
- The system should handle high volumes of notifications efficiently.
- Users must be able to customize their notification settings easily.
- Critical notifications require immediate delivery.
- The system shall track notification delivery status reliably.

## Ambiguities
- **"in a timely manner"**
  Reason: no measurable delivery latency or SLA is defined.
  Resolved by: a specific latency SLA or acceptable delivery window.
  Edge case: notifications arrive too late to be useful, causing missed alerts or stale user actions.
- **"appropriate channels"**
  Reason: the allowed channels and selection rules are not specified.
  Resolved by: an explicit list of supported channels and a channel-selection policy.
  Edge case: a notification is sent only to an unsupported channel or to the wrong channel, so the user never sees it.
- **"based on user preferences"**
  Reason: it is unclear how preferences are stored, prioritized, or resolved when multiple preferences conflict.
  Resolved by: a defined preference schema and precedence rules for conflicting settings.
  Edge case: a user opts into SMS only, but the system also emails them and leaks sensitive content.
- **"handle high volumes of notifications efficiently"**
  Reason: no throughput, scaling, or performance targets are given.
  Resolved by: concrete throughput, concurrency, and latency targets under peak load.
  Edge case: a traffic spike backs up the queue until notifications are delivered hours later or dropped.
- **"easily"**
  Reason: usability expectations are subjective and not testable as written.
  Resolved by: measurable usability or workflow criteria for changing notification settings.
  Edge case: users cannot find or complete the settings change flow, leaving them with unwanted notifications.
- **"Critical notifications"**
  Reason: the criteria for classifying a notification as critical are not defined.
  Resolved by: a rule set or field that marks a notification as critical.
  Edge case: a non-critical message is treated as urgent and interrupts users at the wrong time.
- **"immediate delivery"**
  Reason: no exact delivery window or fallback behavior is stated.
  Resolved by: a maximum acceptable delay and a retry or fallback policy for urgent messages.
  Edge case: a critical alert is delayed long enough that the user misses an outage or security issue.
- **"track notification delivery status reliably"**
  Reason: the required status states, update timing, and reliability guarantees are unspecified.
  Resolved by: a defined set of delivery states, update triggers, and durability/accuracy guarantees.
  Edge case: the UI shows a notification as delivered when it actually failed, preventing support from diagnosing the issue.

- What makes a notification "critical"?
- What is the required delivery window for "immediate delivery"?
- Which delivery status values must be tracked, and what reliability expectations apply?

## Assumptions
- If nobody answers, developers will assume "timely" means best-effort near-real-time delivery without a formal SLA.
- If nobody answers, developers will assume the system supports only the channels already implemented or most commonly used in the product.
- If nobody answers, developers will assume user preferences are a simple per-user configuration with straightforward precedence rules.
- If nobody answers, developers will assume performance should be good enough for expected production traffic but without a published benchmark.
- If nobody answers, developers will assume "easily" means a standard settings UI with no special usability acceptance criteria.
- If nobody answers, developers will assume "critical" notifications are those flagged by the sender or originating service.
- If nobody answers, developers will assume "immediate delivery" means highest-priority dispatch with no intentional delay.
- If nobody answers, developers will assume delivery status tracking includes basic states such as queued, sent, delivered, and failed.

instructions:
# Requirements Review Agent

You turn a raw requirement document into a structured review report held in a
single file, `/analysis.md`.

## Procedure

Work through these stages in order, one tool call per turn. Do not skip a stage
and do not combine two stages into one call.

1. Call `fetch_requirement` to get the requirement document.
2. Call `write_file` to create `/analysis.md` with this exact skeleton, filling
   in only the Confirmed Facts section:

```
# Requirements Analysis

## Confirmed Facts
- one bullet per fact

## Ambiguities

## Clarification Questions

## Assumptions

## Summary
```

3. Call `edit_file` to fill in the Ambiguities section. One bullet per clause, in
   this shape:

```
- **"the exact clause"**
  Reason: why it is under-specified
```

4. Call `edit_file` to fill in the Clarification Questions section. One bullet each.
5. Call `edit_file` to fill in the Assumptions section. One bullet each.
6. Call `edit_file` to fill in the Summary section with two or three sentences.

Tool calls can fail transiently, for example an unreachable external system. If a
tool call returns an error message instead of a result, call the exact same tool
again with the same arguments. This is expected and normal, so keep retrying
until it succeeds.

You never modify the requirement document itself; it is always the source of
truth. You never edit this file either.

Once the Summary is written the review is finished. Reply with one short sentence
confirming completion and call no further tools.

## Review guidance

### Confirmed facts

Record only what the document states directly. Do not infer.

### Ambiguities

Quote the exact clause, then give the reason it is under-specified.

### Clarification questions

Ask what a reviewer would need answered before work could start.

### Assumptions

State what a developer would end up assuming if nobody answered the questions.
